newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain hopes to reform health care in '97-Secretary.
newsitem.headline: Spain hopes to reform health care in '97-Secretary.

text.p: Spanish Social Security Secretary Juan Carlos Aparicio said on Tuesday that he hoped the country could reach a deal to reform the health care system this year.
In an interview with financial daily Gaceta de los Negocios, Aparicio said he feared reform might be delayed because of the difficulty of reaching agreement on the sensitive issue.

"Before implementing the decentralisation process (aimed at giving Spain's regions more financial freedom), it would be necessary to have the general framework of the agreement (in the health system)," he said.
Spain's central government and its regions have to negotiate an expenditure agreement for regions this year.
He added that 60 percent of Spanish citizens have their medical expenditures paid with regional funds.
Spain is living at present above its possibilities and "no generation has the right to do that."
He said Spain is spending 3.5 billion pesetas in interest payments on debt, plus 3.5 billion pesetas for pensions and 3.5 billion pesetas for health care.
